properties.IncidentOverview: A storm moved through northern Harney County on July 22; 2026; yielding hundreds of positive lightning strikes. The Bald Mountain Fire was discovered on the afternoon of July 23; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone; Rangeland Fire Protection Association and the Egypt Fire responded promptly but were unable to contain the fast moving wildfire. Southern Area Team 2 is responsible for management of the fire; along with the Stubble; Crater; Second Flats and Jackass Butte fires. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

A lightning storm moved through Eastern Oregon on July 15; 2026; igniting multiple fires. The Egypt Fire was discovered on the morning of July 16; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone responded promptly but were spread thin due to several other starts in the area. Southern Area Team 2 took command of the Egypt Fire on July 19 at 6 AM. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

The New Pass fire is burning 30 miles northwest of Austin; Nevada; in grass and brush.

An aggressive full-suppression strategy is in place for the Hat Fire to protect communities; structures; critical infrastructure; and other valuable resources at risk. Efforts are focused on minimizing impacts on public; private; and state lands; as well as natural and cultural resources. This is being done in coordination with the local Rangeland Fire Protection Association (RFPA) and cooperating agencies. Current Situation: The perimeter of the Hat Fire remains unchanged and is now 97 percent contained. Yesterday; firefighters focused on mopping up hotspots and extinguishing any burning or smoldering vegetation. Smoke may still be visible from areas within the fire's perimeter where vegetation is burning. Weather and Air Quality: Continued sunny and warm with breezy conditions in the afternoon. Wildfire smoke will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. For more information on Air Quality at your location; visit www.airnow.gov for real-time data. Cooperating Agencies : Juntura RFPA; Owyhee County OEM; Idaho OEM; ODT; ODF; Idaho Power.

properties.Location: 25 Miles CW of Jordan Valley, OR
properties.IncidentOverview: An aggressive full-suppression strategy is in place for the Big Grass Fire to protect communities; structures; critical infrastructure; and other valuable resources at risk. Efforts are focused on minimizing impacts on public; private; and state lands; as well as natural and cultural resources. This is being done in coordination with the local Rangeland Fire Protection Association (RFPA) and cooperating agencies. Current Situation: Yesterday; the Big Grass Fire remained active with continued growth on the east and southeast perimeter. Firefighting efforts were focused on constructing both direct and indirect containment lines (away from the fire’s edge). The indirect containment line is along Flint Creek Road; south to Josephine Road; where it intersects with Mud Flat Road. It continues southeast along Mud Flat Road to Star Ranch Road. The strategy of direct and indirect containment line construction gives firefighters the best chance to fight this fire defensively; especially in areas where the terrain is steep and inaccessible. Today; the primary goal is to keep the fire south of Flint Creek Road. Dozers; hand crews; and engines will continue to seek opportunities to strengthen the direct containment lines and the secondary line along Flint Creek Road. Firefighters will also focus on securing fire lines around ranches; private properties; and critical infrastructure near South Mountain. Further south; efforts will be made to reinforce containment lines along Mud Flat Road. Additionally; a contingency group of firefighting resources has been deployed in the north and south in case they are needed to protect private property. Evacuations: The Owyhee County Sheriff has issued a Level 3 GO evacuation order for Triangle Reservoir; Pleasant Valley; South Mountain; Pleasant Valley Road to the City of Triangle; City of Triangle to the Triangle Reservoir; Flint Creek Road; Juniper Mountain Road; and the west portion of Mud Flat Road. A Level 2 SET status has been issued for Silver City . A Level 1 READY has been issued for the following zones: MAH-E063; MAH-E061; JOJ-E004; and JOJ-E003. BLM Area Closure: Access to the North Fork Campground along Juniper Mountain Road in Owyhee County is temporarily closed. The entire area south of Trout Creek Road and Silver City Road to the East Fork and Main Stem of the Owyhee River and from the Oregon border east to Highway 78 and Highway 51 is also temporarily closed. These closures are necessary to ensure the safety of both the public and firefighters involved in suppression efforts. Weather and Air Quality: Continued sunny and warm with breezy conditions. Wildfire smoke will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. For more information on Air Quality at your location; visit www.airnow.gov for real-time data. Cooperating Agencies: Jordan Valley RFPA; Owyhee RFPA; Malheur County Sheriff’s Office; Owyhee County Sheriff’s Office; Owyhee County OEM; Idaho OEM; ODT; Idaho Power; Idaho Department of Lands.

The Ward Fire began on July 31; 2026 near Ward Mountain; approximately nine miles south of Ely; Nevada. The fire is burning in sagebrush; pinyon‑juniper; and mixed conifer fuels in steep and rugged terrain. The fire is being managed under a full‑suppression strategy. Resources from federal; state; local; and cooperating agencies are working to limit fire spread and protect values at risk. A combination of ground and aerial firefighting tactics is being used to slow movement through difficult terrain and support containment efforts. Priorities for the incident include firefighter and public safety; protection of private lands; and safeguarding critical infrastructure in the surrounding area.
